symptom: A change data capture service tracking an association with owner Both passed check and exec, then mx check failed CE1583 ('the associated entity … must also be included', at the Entity change source) even though that entity was in the service. A tracked association whose other end was not in the service failed the same way (at the Association property). MDL could not express the fix: naming the association on the TO entity was refused with 'is not an attribute or an association of Tag'.
file: mdl/backend/modelsdk/cdc_write.go resolveCdcMember; mdl/executor/validate_cdc_associations.go (MDL-CDC01), wired in cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go
cause: resolveCdcMember accepted an association only from its FROM entity (ParentID). Studio Pro's CDC editor offers an entity every association it OWNS (getAllAssociations(e).filter(isOwnerOf)), so a both-owned association belongs to both sides, and mxbuild wants it tracked from both. Nothing at check time looked at associations in a CDC service.
fix: resolveCdcMember also accepts an owner Both association from its TO entity; that member's baseline AssociatedEntityGuid points back at the FROM entity, with multiplicity OneToOne. MDL-CDC01 (an error, check -p) reports a tracked association whose other end is not a source, and an owner Both association tracked from one side only. It reads associations from the project and from the script.
insight: CE1583's rule lives in compiled .NET, so measure it with mx check rather than read it: two variants on a blank 11.17.0 project settled it. One side gave CE1583; both sides gave 0 errors and no CE1585, which also confirmed that the TO-side baseline mxcli writes matches Studio Pro's. Re-running the both-sides script writes nothing.
